newsitem.title: USA: Chicago committee OKs issue for Catholic school.
newsitem.headline: Chicago committee OKs issue for Catholic school.

text.p: The Chicago City Council Finance Committee on Monday approved a controversial $7 million bond issue for a Catholic high school, according to a spokesman for the committee.
The conduit financing now heads to the full city council meeting scheduled for Wednesday, the committee spokesman said.

The debt issue for De La Salle High School continued to raise questions about the separation of church and state, particularly by a representative of the American Civil Liberties Union, according to local news reports.

Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer, has said the variable-rate note deal would be the first conduit financing by the city for a religious school and would be backed by a letter of credit from Northern Trust Bank.
George K. Baum & Co is the sole manager for the deal.
